overview: The OTAG-433 module provides a means for any electronic device to implement low-cost wireless connectivity. The module operates on the 434 MHz custom band with a proprietary protocol.

It is ideal for applications where longer battery life and range are required. The module is built around the Silicon Labs EZR32HG220 wireless MCU family, combining an ARM Cortex-M0+ with a sub-GHz radio and an energy-efficient 32-bit microcontroller with 64 kB of flash. The architecture isolates the wireless software without sacrificing RF performance or security for applications.

A rich set of hardware peripherals such as GPIO, UART and timers, low transmit and receive currents, ultra-low-power standby and sleep modes, fast wake-up time and an AES accelerator with 128-bit keys make it a great choice for battery-oriented applications, and it supports deployment of dense networks with long coverage.
